title: Wall Street money shifts from HYPE ETF to ETH ETF: BeInCrypto
summary: Wall Street capital appears to be moving out of the HYPE ETF and into spot Ethereum ETFs, which have posted net inflows for three straight weeks, according to a BeInCrypto analysis. The outlet said Ethereum saw net inflows of $84 million, $105 million and $103.9 million over the past three weeks, while Hyperliquid posted net outflows for two consecutive weeks. It added that the HYPE ETF’s weekly trading volume fell to $62.7 million, the lowest level since its May launch. BeInCrypto said institutional money is currently flowing into ETH more actively than BTC, while inflows into major altcoin ETFs such as XRP and SOL remain limited. It added, "HYPE ETF" is the only one seeing money leave, which suggests weakening investor sentiment.

title: Latest CLARITY draft includes white-hat hacker incentive provision
summary: The latest draft of the CLARITY bill includes a provision on an incentive program for white-hat hackers and security researchers, Bitcoin News reported. The media outlet added the provision calls for a program to formally encourage and reward their work, with the aim of strengthening protection for digital asset infrastructure by offering compensation for public-interest activities such as identifying vulnerabilities, providing information to help track hackers, and supporting the recovery of stolen assets.

title: AFX Trader hacker swaps 655.4 ETH for 18.86 BTC via THORChain
summary: The hacker behind the AFX Trader exploit swapped 655.4 ETH for 18.86 BTC through THORChain, EmberCN reported. On July 23, the Arbitrum-based protocol AFX Trader lost $24.15 million in USDC in a bridge hack, and the attacker later swapped those funds into 12,467.4 ETH. AFX had also proposed a white-hat negotiation under which the hacker could legally keep the remaining 30% of the stolen funds in exchange for returning 70% of the assets.

title: Shenzhen authorities shut down multiple crypto-related self-media accounts
summary: Chinese regulators in Shenzhen have identified and shut down multiple self-media accounts for violating rules related to virtual assets, according to China’s People’s Daily. The report said several government bodies, including the Shenzhen branch of the People’s Bank of China, the Shenzhen Securities Regulatory Bureau, the Shenzhen Cyberspace Administration Office, and the Shenzhen Local Financial Administration, recently carried out a joint special crackdown on financial information online. During the operation, authorities found violations by multiple crypto-related self-media accounts, including "搜搜比特币." The accounts were found to have promoted virtual asset-related businesses to users in China and encouraged public participation in illegal financial activities tied to virtual assets. Shenzhen authorities added they plan to keep tightening oversight of online financial information and crack down on activities that fuel virtual asset speculation or involve illegal investment recommendations in order to maintain financial market order.

title: 224 crypto hacks caused $1.32B in losses in the first half of 2026
summary: A total of 224 cryptocurrency hacking incidents were recorded in the first half of this year, with losses reaching about $1.32 billion, according to Onchain Lens. The main attack types included access control vulnerabilities, phishing, and oracle-related exploits. Among them, large losses were concentrated in attacks involving privilege escalation and administrator account takeovers tied to access control weaknesses. KelpDAO and Drift Protocol were among the hardest hit, suffering losses of $292 million and $280 million, respectively.
author: @CoinnessGL
